name: GGUF Q2_K / Q2_K_S (2-bit K-quant)
bits: 2.625 effective bpw for block_q2_K (source comment); 2.9697 measured avg for Q2_K_S and 3.1593 for plain Q2_K on Llama-3.1-8B (llama.cpp quantize README)
kernels: ggml-cuda mul_mat_vec_q / dequantize_mul_mat_vec + convert_mul_mat (per-type, not mixed-type aware)
quality_delta: Only the unified Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct study was found for the 2-bit K-quant tier. The closest measured point is Q3_K_S (3.9960 bpw, same family): WikiText-2 ppl 8.96 vs 7.32 FP16, GSM8K 68.31 vs 77.63, IFEval 71.87 vs 78.93, unweighted 5-benchmark mean 65.49 vs 69.47 (quant-gguf-kquant-study). No published perplexity for plain Q2_K/Q2_K_S was located, so none recorded.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-10-04: was 256. 256 is the SUPER-BLOCK size (QK_K), not the scale-sharing group. dequantize_row_q2_K applies one (scale,min) pair per 16 values (`dl = d*(sc & 0xF); ml = min*(sc>>4); for l<16`), 16 sub-blocks per 256-value super-block, each sub-block's 4-bit scale and 4-bit min themselves sitting on the fp16 d/dmin super-block scales. Q2_K is the plain (non-mixed) 2-bit k-quant; Q2_K_S is the mixed variant. BIT LAYOUT, verified from ggml/src/ggml-common.h (not from any blog): the K-quant super-block is QK_K = 256 values. block_q2_K = { uint8_t scales[QK_K/16];  // 16 scales AND 16 mins, 4-bit each, packed 2 per byte = 16 bytes uint8_t qs[QK_K/4];      // 64 bytes of 2-bit quants ggml_half d;            // super-block scale FOR THE QUANTIZED SCALES ggml_half dmin; }       // super-block scale FOR THE QUANTIZED MINS }.  So it is 16 blocks of 16 elements, each block x = a*q + b with a and b both 4-bit quantized and themselves scaled by fp16 d/dmin: 64 bytes quants + 16 bytes scales/mins + 4 bytes fp16 = 84 bytes per 256 values = 2.625 bpw, matching the header comment. This is the two-level-scale design that distinguishes the k-quants: the per-16 scale is not fp16 like legacy q4_0, it is 4-bit and sits on a second fp16 scale. MIXTURE (from src/llama-quant.cpp): Q2_K is not a single type. attn_v -> Q4_K if n_gqa>=4 else Q3_K; ffn_down -> Q3_K; attn_output -> Q3_K. Q2_K_S additionally bumps ffn_down in the first n_layer/8 layers to Q4_K and, if n_gqa>=4, attn_v to Q4_K. For the plain Q2_K, ffn_down is forced to Q3_K and attn_output to Q3_K - i.e. 'Q2_K' is genuinely ~3.16 bpw despite the name. Weight-only: activations stay fp16/bf16 at runtime, so there is no 2-bit-activation hardware claim to make. ggml has a bespoke dequantize_row_q2_K + mul_mat kernel per backend but no accelerator has a GGUF k-quant path in silicon; everything is dequantized on the fly. vLLM labels its GGUF support experimental/under-optimized and positions it as a memory-footprint tool.
